tier_reason: First-party results from public benchmark code (bm/bm_parse.cpp, bm/bm_emit.cpp, yaml-cpp/libyaml/libfyaml pulled in by bm/CMakeLists.txt); compiler is stated (gcc 16.1, Release, per the results .md build path and the readthedocs page) but no CPU model and no explicit flags beyond a CMake Release build, so not A; not an independent suite, so not B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'ryml parses at ~200MB/s and emits at ~600MB/s, and is generally 30x (parse) / 150x (emit) faster than yamlcpp, and never less than 10x (parse) / 50x (emit)'. Linked travis.yml parse data: ryml variants 163.41-358.98 MB/s (13.96x-30.66x) vs yamlcpp_arena 11.71 MB/s (1.00x); libyaml_arena 86.79 MB/s (7.41x), libfyaml_arena 62.47 MB/s (5.34x), so ryml is several times faster than libyaml on this file (derived from page data). Linked travis.yml emit data: ryml_yaml_str 1608.06 MB/s (142.69x) vs yamlcpp 11.27 MB/s.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 16.1, CMake Release build, C++17 (build directory 'linux-x86_64-gxx16.1-Release-17' in ryml-bm-parse-travis.md; readthedocs 'Is it rapid' page says 'This section shows results using gcc 16.1'; Windows results use Visual Studio 2026). Explicit optimization/arch flags are not stated.
corrections.hardware: CPU model not stated. The google-benchmark context in ryml-bm-parse-travis.json shows a local machine (host 'bach', 20 CPUs @ 4279 MHz, L1d 32 KiB, L2 1 MiB shared by 2, L3 ~19.25 MiB, CPU scaling disabled), not Travis/AppVeyor CI runners.
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers from the author's own machine (the 'travis'/'appveyor' in result file names are the input files bm/cases/travis.yml and appveyor.yml, not CI runners). The CPU model is never named and flags beyond a CMake Release build are not given, so the tier is capped at C despite public, runnable benchmark code. The README's 'never less than 10x (parse)' is slightly overstated: the linked parse scatter data shows scalar_dquot_multiline at 9.73x vs yaml-cpp. The 0.16.0-pre result JSON records executable 'ryml-bm-parse-0.15.2' dated 2026-07-07. Independent success stories (rATHENA 10x-70x, OpenXcom 67x, CERN LHCb memory drop) corroborate large speedups over yaml-cpp.

notes: Numbers match the linked results file and README. The record misread the result filenames as Travis/AppVeyor CI runs; hardware and compiler fields are corrected from the result .json/.md. last_commit was the repo pushed_at date (2026-09-24); the default-branch head is 2026-09-06.

tier_reason: README benchmark table (SpeedyXml 0.34 s vs libxml2 SAX2 1.53 s, 4.4x) comes from public benchmark code (tools/CmpOtherParsers.cpp via tools/benchmark.cmake, tools/public_bench.sh), but no compiler, flags, or CPU model are stated for the published results, so the tier is first-party C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README table, 235 MiB real-world document, single core: SpeedyXml 0.34 s vs libxml2 (streaming SAX2) 1.53 s (4.4x), pugixml DOM 1.00 s (2.9x), RapidXml DOM in-situ 1.29 s (3.7x), Expat 4.38 s (12.7x); 'That is ~680 MiB/s'. README chart over 8 public datasets ('no other parser reaches half of SpeedyXml's throughput on any document') puts libxml2 at 6-29% of SpeedyXml's throughput, i.e. roughly 3.4x-17x slower (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the published results; tools/public_bench.sh builds the bench tool with CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release and the system default compiler.
corrections.caveats: No CPU model, compiler, or flags are given for the README numbers, and the 235 MiB document is unnamed and not published (the 8 public datasets in the chart are reproducible via tools/public_bench.sh). The bench tool times each parser once per run with gettimeofday wall clock, in a fixed order with SpeedyXml last. The pugixml/RapidXml rows are DOM vs streaming, as the author notes. The libxml2 comparison is streaming vs streaming, but SpeedyXml does less work: UTF-8 only, no namespace resolution, no DTD entities, not validating, text entities not decoded. Very new (created 2026-07-27), 1-star project with no third-party corroboration.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly, and the benchmark code is public. Public-dataset ratios were read from the README SVG chart (bar order SpeedyXml, PugiXml, RapidXml, Expat, LibXml2 per tools/gen_bench_chart.py). Metadata (BSD-3-Clause, not fork, 1 star, last commit 2026-07-29, active) is confirmed.
